newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bezeq Israel to lower some prices.
newsitem.headline: Bezeq Israel to lower some prices.

text.p: Bezeq Israel Telecom, the state-controlled phone company, will lower its prices for international phone calls to compete with two new operators, company president Issac Kaul said on Thursday.
"It will be an interesting competition," Kaul said in an interview with Israel Radio.
He noted that Bezeq had set up a subsidiary to operate international phone service.
"I can't promise we will have lower prices (than the other operators) but we will be competitive," he said.
On Wednesday, the Communications Ministry announced that two multinational groups had won licences to operate international phone services from Israel.
The two consortia, comprising Israeli and foreign companies, will begin services in about seven months.

Although Bezeq stands to lose a big chunk of the $700 million international call market, this will be partly offset by interconnection and user fees the new operators will have to pay to it. A third of Bezeq's revenues and nearly half of its profits derive from international service.
A ministry official said the price of a one-minute call to the United States at peak hours would fall to 0.62 to 0.65 shekel a minute, compared with Bezeq's current rate of 3.53 shekels.

The first winning group includes Italy's STET, SBC Communications (formerly Southwestern Bell) of the United States and three Israeli companies - Globescom, the Kahan Group and Aureq, a joint venture of SBC and Kahan.
The second is led by Clalcom, a subsidiary of Israel's Clal Industries, and includes Sprint Corp, Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Israel's Matav Cable Systems Media Ltd.
